summary: PyTorch library for graph neural networks, with many ready-made GNN layers and datasets for learning on networks and other graph data.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: PyG (PyTorch Geometric) is a library built on PyTorch for writing and training graph neural networks (GNNs), models that learn from data shaped as graphs such as social networks, citation networks, molecules or 3D meshes. It ships implementations of most state-of-the-art GNN architectures from published papers, common datasets, and a message passing API for building your own layers. It also supports large graphs with millions of nodes, dynamic graphs and heterogeneous graphs.
sixtySeconds.problem: Graph data doesn't fit normal neural network layers. PyG provides the building blocks to train models on graphs with a PyTorch-style API.
whoFor: Data scientists with network or molecule data
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Pick it for the widest set of GNN models in PyTorch with an API that feels like plain PyTorch.

overview: Since PyG 2.3, pip install torch_geometric is enough; only PyTorch is required.
Optional extensions (pyg-lib, torch-scatter, torch-sparse) add speed and extra features; install them later from the PyG wheel index matching your PyTorch and CUDA versions.
Start with the README's 2-layer GCN on the Cora citation dataset. It is MIT licensed.
